title: [Bugs] SM policy leaked on every failure path after NewUeSmPolicyData; error response omits Location so the SMF can never delete it
body:
## Bug Description
`HandleCreateSmPolicyRequest` registers a new SM policy into `UeContext.SmPolicyData` at line 116, then continues with work that can fail. The failure exit after that returns without removing the entry, and the error response carries no `Location` header.

The paired release, `HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest`, is a separate N7 request the SMF sends using the id from `Location`. Without that id the entry can never be released, by the handler or by anyone else. The key is supi-pduSessionId, so each failure on a new PDU session id adds an entry, and a later create with the same id overwrites it. Entries accumulate up to one per PDU session id per UE (at most 15).

The failure exit sits behind `PCFContext.GetTokenCtx` and is taken whenever the NRF is unavailable at that point. Only the success exit returns `Location`.

**Acquire at L116.** The entry goes into the per-UE map. Note L113 right above it: a `delete` already exists here, used to clear a stale entry before overwriting.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L112-L116

```go
if smPolicyData != nil {
    delete(ue.SmPolicyData, smPolicyID)      // L113
}
smPolicyData = ue.NewUeSmPolicyData(smPolicyID, request, &smData)   // L116: acquire
```

**Release is a separate N7 request.** `HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest` (L516) is reached by `POST /sm-policies/{smPolicyId}/delete`, and the SMF only learns `smPolicyId` from the `Location` header of the `201`. No `Location`, no release.

**The failure exit after L116 does not delete or send `Location`:**

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L380-L385

```go
ctx, pd, err := p.Context().GetTokenCtx(models.ServiceName_NUDR_DR, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_UDR)
if err != nil {
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, pd.Cause)
    c.JSON(int(pd.Status), pd)
    return                                   // ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID] still set
}
```

`GetTokenCtx`: with `oauth: true` it does a live NRF fetch, so any NRF outage at L380 takes that exit. It sits *after* the acquire, while the earlier UDR lookup sits *before* it, so an outage beginning after the UE's policy data is cached passes the earlier lookup and fails here.

Separately, `util.GetProblemDetail` does not populate `Status`, so `c.JSON(int(problemDetails.Status), ...)` is `c.JSON(0, ...)` and gin emits **HTTP 200** with a ProblemDetails body. A client checking only the status code treats the failed create as a success.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, PCF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`. A probe in the PCF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports `len(ue.SmPolicyData)` across `UePool`, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak: one line decides it.** Three runs, same requests, `pduSessionId` incrementing so each one gets a distinct `smPolicyID`. B and C use a build-time hook (`LEAK_FAULT`, inert when unset) to force a failure, the only difference being whether it fires one line after L116 or one line before:

| | failure point | requests | HTTP | entries held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, normal | none | 500 | `201` + `Location` | 500, then **0** after 500 deletes |
| B, fails *after* L116 | one line after acquire | 2000 | error, no `Location` | **2000** |
| C, fails *before* L116 | one line above | 2000 | error, no `Location` | **0** |

A shows the pair works. C shows that a failing request is not by itself a problem. B differs from C only in whether the acquire had already run.

**Accumulation, run B:**

| requests | entries held | heap objects |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 18,900 |
| 250 | 250 | 37,362 |
| 500 | 500 | 45,403 |
| 1000 | 1000 | 61,548 |
| 1500 | 1500 | 77,168 |
| 2000 | 2000 | 92,725 |

Slope exactly 1 per request. The PCF does not validate pduSessionId, so the test goes past the 15 values a real SMF would send; in practice the bound is 15 per UE. A forced `runtime.GC()` leaves the count at 2000 and `heap_alloc` at 8.7 MB; run C stayed flat at ~7 MB over the same 2000 requests.

Deleting by guessed id (`.../sm-policies/imsi-208930000000001-1/delete`) returns `204` and drops the count 2000 → 1997, so the release logic is fine. A real SMF simply never received those ids.

**Reaching L384 without the hook.** With `oauth: true`, 300 policies were created normally, the NRF was killed, and the same 300 creates repeated. All 300 returned **HTTP 500 with no `Location`**, the `GetTokenCtx` exit, with the acquire at L116 already done. (Same keys, so this run shows reachability rather than growth; growth is what B measures.)

Killing the NRF *before* the UE's policy data is cached instead gives `400 Can't find UE SM Policy Data in UDR` from the UDR lookup above L116, which does not leak, consistent with C.

## Expected Behavior
When the create fails after the acquire at L116, the handler should remove the `ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]` entry before returning (as L113 already does before overwriting), so a failed create does not leave a permanent entry that no `Location`-bearing response ever lets the SMF release. The error response should also carry a correct HTTP status rather than a `0`/`200` from an unpopulated `Status`.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (PCF v1.4.3, `df6c0da`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    HTTP 500, no Location header (GetTokenCtx exit, acquire at L116 already done)
    400 Can't find UE SM Policy Data in UDR   (when NRF killed before policy data cached — does not leak)

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF on loopback.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The failure exit at L380 sits *after* the acquire at L116, while the earlier UDR lookup sits *before* it. An outage beginning after the UE's policy data is cached passes the earlier lookup and fails at `GetTokenCtx`, leaving the entry registered. The key includes `pduSessionId`, so entries accumulate one per failed request, bounded at 15 per UE in practice.

## Additional Context
Every create that fails after L116 leaves a permanent `SmPolicyData` entry: not reclaimable by GC, not deletable by the SMF because the failure response omits `Location`. The reachable trigger is NRF unavailability during `GetTokenCtx`. For the duration of an outage every create that gets past the earlier UDR lookup adds an entry, and the SMF sees only a `500`.

Entries hold `PolicyDecision`, both id generators and the GBR remainders, roughly 37 heap objects each. There is no eviction, no timeout and no sweep over `SmPolicyData`, so an entry is removed only by a PCF restart, a later create with the same supi-pduSessionId, or an operator guessing that id.

## How did we find?
We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.
